articleTitle: Prediction of Surface Roughness and Hardness on Multi 3D Printers with Machine Learning
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM), known as 3D Printing, is the “process of joining materials to make objects from 3D model data, usually layer upon layer.” Quality control in 3D printing is challenging, particularly in controlling surface roughness and hardness values of printed objects. This research aims to create predictive modeling using machine learning algorithms to predict surface roughness and hardness values. Data obtained from experimental testing of various printing parameters will be used as a dataset to train and test the predictive model. The results of this study show that there are differences in surface roughness and hardness values from variations of 3D printers. For the Ender 3 V3 KE 3D Printer, the average surface roughness and hardness values are $9.83 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ and 72.41 HD, respectively. Meanwhile, for the Flashforge Creator Pro KE 3D Printer, the average surface roughness and hardness values are $7.02 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ and 73.2 HD, respectively. To predict surface roughness with the highest accuracy, the XGBoost method has the lowest percentage error based on MAPE at 15.16%, while for hardness values, the Random Forest method has the lowest percentage error based on MAPE at 3.34%. The implementation of the developed predictive model is applied in a UI system to optimize printing parameters to achieve the desired quality in terms of surface roughness and hardness.

articleTitle: Generalized Huber Loss Function and Gradient Flow Designed Fixed-Time Convergence Trajectory Tracking Controller for Quadcopter
abstract: In this paper, a trajectory tracking controller for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is proposed. The gradient flow method is utilized to design the controller which can make position and velocity errors converge to zero in fixed-time with concise form of equation. In the controller, desired velocity error formula from position error is designed to be a first layer of fixed-time convergence; an error exists between real and desired, which thus needs a second layer of fixed-time convergence to control the error to zero. A generalized Huber loss function combines the advantages of quadratic loss and absolute loss function to increases the stability of the proposed controller in this paper. Several numerical simulations are performed and prove the feasibility and effectiveness of the design.

articleTitle: A Case of Cups and a Ball: Utilizing Generative Artificial Intelligence for Human-robotic Collaboration in Task Execution
abstract: Within the domain of robotics, effective interaction between a human collaborator and robot is a topic of great importance. With the continued advancements in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI), we propose a prototype system that utilizes GAI and seeks to bridge the gap between the human and robot. This prototype utilizes a Large Language Model (LLM) combined with a vision system for detection and tracking, to allow the GAI system to control a robotic arm and manipulate objects within the action space. We model the action space within our experiments on the 3-cup Monte game where the user can prompt the system to manipulate the cups within the action space based on the ball’s location. Experimentation is done on prompts of varying lengths of sequences, and we evaluate our system based on its ability to understand the prompt and correctly execute the desired task. With this collaboration of techniques and technologies, we hope to open the possibilities and extend human and robotic collaboration into new areas. The results of our experiments show promising results to this end.

articleTitle: A Monitoring and Control System Based on Image Recognition for Iron Filings Cleaning of CNC Machine Tools
abstract: This study addresses a key challenge in the CNC tool machining industry: automated in-machine chip removal. Initially, we designed and manufactured an innovative nozzle, incorporating elastic plastic hoses to replace sections of traditional hard coil pipes. A 3D-printed auxiliary mechanism was developed to enable the servo motor to direct the nozzle to any specified coordinates on a two-dimensional plane. Simultaneously, captured images are divided into multiple subblocks for detailed analysis. Image recognition algorithms process each block to determine the location of iron filings. The ratio of detected iron filings is then computed to establish cleaning priorities, which the embedded system uses to direct the servo motor for effective cleaning. Additionally, the system features a human-machine interface that monitors the cleaning process, providing on-site personnel with real-time insights into the machine’s internal conditions. Experimental results from a custom simulation environment demonstrate that the system efficiently reduces the accumulation of iron filings on the platform to levels below the set threshold within a short time frame. This research aims to minimize machine tool idle time, lower personnel costs, and enhance overall production capacity.

articleTitle: Environmental Sound Recognition based on a STM32 SensorTile board
abstract: Recently, with the development of the artificial intelligence (AI). The application of Deep Learning is expending into different field. Image recognition, personalized recommendations in search engines, Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Speech Recognition are based on the Deep Learning. The continued development and integration of these applications can also lead to a more convenient lifestyle. Including Autonomous Vehicle, Facial Recognition and more. Based on the structure of Deep Learning. We transfer the data of the ambient sound into the Log-Mel spectrogram. Then using the Log-Mel spectrogram to train the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model. After this, we deployed the trained model onto the STM32 SensorTile board for experimentation.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Robot with Autonomous for Garbage Collection and Compression
abstract: This research focuses on developing an intelligent robot for garbage collection and recycling compression. The robot is flexible usage for both autonomous and remote control. With advanced machine vision and image recognition, the robot can identify different types of garbage and follows a fixed route to collect garbage. It has an electric linear actuator for efficient compression and offers safe and flexible control. The most advantage is that the robot is fully electrified, simpler and smaller than a hydraulic system. This research demonstrates a mechatronic system integration with theoretical analysis, concept development, system design, and control flow. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the prototype robot indifferent environments.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Navigation System Based on the Integration of Inertial Navigation System/Positioning System
abstract: The objective of this paper is to integrate the inertial navigation system (INS) and positioning system for determining the position, velocity, and attitude of a moving object. In this paper, the Kalman filter is used for sensor fusion. In the experiments, the sensor fusion algorithm is implemented through a digital signal processor (DSP). To assess the performance of the algorithm, a linear slide with a magnetic linear scale and a three-axis rotational calibration platform are used in the restricted-range movement. The results of experiments show that this developed system can achieve an update rate of 800 Hz and compensate the latency of the positioning system. Furthermore, the sensor fusion algorithm can provide accurate three-axis position, three-axis velocity, roll angle, and pitch angle. However, there is noticeable drifting in the yaw angle.

articleTitle: Quaternion-Based Attitude Tracking Control Design for UAVs
abstract: This paper utilizes quaternions to represent the attitude of UAVs and proposes an attitude controller. We use backstepping methodology together with fractional exponent to achieve salient performance in tracking a desired attitude trajectory. Numerical simulation results are provided to verify the presented scheme and demonstrate itseffectiveness.

articleTitle: Design and Verification of the Control Algorithm of an Anti-Lock Braking System for Commercial Motorcycles
abstract: This paper proposes an anti-lock brake system (ABS) designed to enhance braking efficiency and maneuverability for motorcycles. The proposed ABS independently controls the braking pressure at each wheel, which helps prevent the rider from falling during emergency braking situations. It has been installed on a commercial motorcycle to verify its functionality. Several tests were conducted to assess the braking performance on both uniform and uneven road surfaces. The results demonstrate that the proposed ABS accurately adjusts the braking pressure at each wheel, prevents wheel lock-up, and maintains the motorcycle’s controllability during emergency braking. The system meets regulatory requirements for all tests. Emergency braking maneuvers will become safer and more efficient through the use of advanced safety techniques in anti-lock braking systems.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Voice Production System for Deaf and Mute Individuals Combining Lip-reading and Text-to-Speech Technologies
abstract: In modern society, deaf and mute individuals face significant challenges in social and daily communication due to their limitations in speech expression. Although traditional assistive tools have made some progress in addressing the hearing impairments of these individuals, there remains a significant lack of support in speech expression. However, with the rapid development of deep learning technology, new opportunities have emerged. We have developed an innovative wearable vocal device that combines lip recognition technology and text-to-speech (TTS) technology based on a deep learning framework to identify messages by analyzing lip movements and morphology, which are then converted into text and subsequently transformed into speech output through TTS. This allows users to communicate orally with others. By modifying the basic unit of the dataset, our model has demonstrated an accuracy rate of $95 \%$. Additionally, this technology can be applied in various scenarios, such as helping patients with speech difficulties communicate with doctors who do not know sign language, or as a mobile lip reading input method, which serves as an alternative to voice input while protecting user privacy. We aim to provide more technological support to the deaf and mute community, promoting an accessible experience in their social and daily interactions.

articleTitle: Road Slope Estimation Using Field-Adjustable Stereo Vision
abstract: Modern vehicles rely on springs or hydraulic pistons to absorb road irregularities. Accurately estimating road surface height can greatly enhance a robot’s navigation ability. This paper proposes an improved camera setup, using an adjustable-angle camera to capture more comprehensive road surface data, with real-time correction reducing errors to $1-2 \%$ and maintaining 60 FPS. The system converts 2 D images into 3D point cloud data and introduces a method for calculating translation matrix parameters, improving data correction accuracy. Results show significant improvements in detecting slopes, especially downhill, and the system adapts to terrain changes, enhancing the safety of autonomous driving.

articleTitle: Multi-Robot Active Mapping based on Inverse Reinforcement Learning in Unknown Environments
abstract: Multi-robot active mapping aims to efficiently explore and construct complete maps of unknown environments using multiple robots. The key to solving this problem lies in frontier-based exploration, which enables more efficient robot movements. Recent approaches have employed Reinforcement Learning (RL) to optimize robot policies for efficient exploration. However, designing a suitable reward function for $R L$ in this context is challenging because it requires balancing multiple objectives, such as rapid exploration, efficient coordination, and complete coverage. To address this challenge, we propose an Inverse Reinforcement Learning (IRL) approach that automatically updates the underlying reward function from expert demonstrations of effective multi-robot mapping. We use the performance of NeuralCoMapping on specific maps as expert demonstrations and take NeuralCoMapping as the RL policy. By learning the potential reward function optimized by these expert demonstrations, we aim to discover a more comprehensive and balanced reward function that captures the key features of efficient multi-robot mapping. The proposed IRL-based approach not only offers a promising direction for automatically learning effective reward functions and policies in complex multi-robot systems but also instills optimism for the future of robotics, reducing the need for manual reward engineering.

articleTitle: Fixed-Time Convergence of Attitude Control for Quadrotors Using Quaternion and Gradient Flow Method
abstract: This paper discusses the application of quaternion representation in attitude control for quadrotor UAVs. We use a fixed-time gradient flow method to design its dynamic equations, proving that the attitude error can converge to the desired outcome. Simulations are conducted to implement the fixed-time gradient flow and demonstrate the feasibility of this design.

articleTitle: Trajectory tracking control of a mobile robot
abstract: This is a practical paper, mainly implementing a trajectory tracking mobile robot. The wheels of the mobile robot are omnidirectional wheels, and the controller are a Raspberry Pi single-board computer and a motor-driven expansion board. The mobile robot connects a high-resolution camera via USB. This paper uses OpenCV to perform image processing functions and uses PID to control the movement of the robot. The PID controller parameters are adjusted using the rule of thumb to reduce overshoot. The Raspberry Pi single-board computer and motor drive expansion board can control the speed of the left and right motors, and can also control the camera’s pan and tilt, allowing it to adjust the camera angle and adjust the experimental conditions. According to the experimental results, trajectory tracking is successfully completed.

articleTitle: A Trajectory Tracking Control Design for UAVs Using Fractional Exponent Integral Sliding Mode Method
abstract: In this paper, we will design a controller for trajectory tracking control applying on unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). We use Fractional Exponent Integral Sliding Mode Control to decide our ideal control, generate appropriate output to make the position error can reach to zero. The method we use can keep the variable original. In this way, the output generated by controller can make convergence more accurate and faster. The experiment results show the practicality of this method, but also demonstrate the direction. Besides there is also some shortcomings need to be improved.

articleTitle: Real-Time Obstacle Distance Measurement Independent of Illumination with Monocular Camera and Cross Laser
abstract: Natural disasters have sudden and significant impacts on lives and property. To mitigate these effects, the deployment of autonomous disaster robots is increasingly seen as a critical component of efficient disaster response. A key technology in this context is obstacle detection, essential for autonomous navigation. This paper proposes a novel method utilizing a monocular camera and laser light to detect obstacles by capturing laser light features. This approach offers high reliability and cost-effectiveness, making it well-suited for disaster robot operations. However, the accuracy of distance measurement can be affected by illuminance, especially in bright environments, where the previous methods were primarily designed for use in low-light conditions. Therefore, in this study, a distance measurement method that is independent of illuminance and can accurately measure distances even in bright environments was devised. Specifically, when extracting the laser light, binarization processing was performed using YUV, a color space report that can consider luminance and hue separately, and similar parts were searched for and extracted from the laser light shape by template matching. The system succeeded in detecting obstacles with a maximum error difference of 1.3 cm.

articleTitle: High Efficient Step-up DC-DC Converter With Zero Current Switching And Voltage Multiplier Cell
abstract: This paper proposes a DC-DC high step-up converter featuring zero-current switching (ZCS) and a voltage multiplier cell. The converter is primarily based on a conventional boost circuit, integrating coupled inductors and a switched-capacitor-based voltage multiplier unit. By utilizing the leakage inductance of the coupled inductor and a capacitor to form a resonant circuit, the resonant principle enables zero-current switching of the switching components within the voltage multiplier unit during turn-off. This effectively reduces switching losses, particularly when enhancing the step-up ratio of the converter.

articleTitle: Improved Pulse Voltage Injection Method for Initial Position Estimation in Surface-Mounted Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
abstract: When the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) is at a standstill, an improved pulse voltage injection technique is employed. This method involves sequentially injecting short-duration, high-frequency pulse voltages with sufficient amplitude into different phases of the stator windings. This process induces significant magnetization, leading to magnetic saturation effects. The varying degrees of magnetic saturation cause different current responses, which can then be used to infer the relative position between the rotor and stator, thereby estimating the initial rotor position.

articleTitle: Labeling Correction in Optical Inspection of Surface Mount Technology Assembly Through Data Cleaning Using StableDiffusionXL Combined with Contrastive Learning
abstract: Labeling errors were identified in the dataset collected from automated optical inspection during the Surface Mount Technology (SMT) assembly process. This paper presents a data cleaning process to correct these errors. To effectively reduce error rates in SMT production and improve product quality, it is essential to build a dataset encompassing various types of components, as printed circuit board panels contain more than one type of part. Leveraging this dataset, combined with state of the art image models, allows for precise classification of different components, significantly enhancing production quality and efficiency. The process uses contrastive learning for model training and StableDiffusionXL (SDXL) for image generation. Contrastive learning improves model performance by highlighting sample differences, while SDXL generates images when comparison samples are unavailable. And two experiments were conducted for testing. The first experiment used a prepared test dataset consisting of $\mathbf{2, 0 0 0}$ pairs of images, with 1,000 labeled as good and 1,000 labeled as defective, resulting in a balanced dataset. The results show that using our proposed method, the highest accuracy achieved with SDXL assistance was $73.45 \%$, while without SDXL, the highest accuracy reached $\mathbf{9 4 . 7 0 \%}$. The second experiment compared the difference between manual methods and our method, showing that our method achieved an overkill rate of $2.9 \%$ and a leakage rate of $1.2 \%$.

articleTitle: A Novel Cutting Fluids Performance Assurance System for CNC Machine Tools
abstract: In the CNC machine tool industry, cutting fluid is a crucial component of the machining process. Nevertheless, as the duration of cutting fluid use increases, its performance progressively deteriorates, presenting a significant challenge that necessitates resolution. This study introduces an innovative intelligent monitoring system designed to optimize the preparation of cutting fluid in CNC machine tools. The aim is to extend the fluid’s service life, mitigate tool wear, and address issues arising from fluid degradation. The system integrates a heating plate, sensors, pumping motors, and embedded systems to monitor and manage the cutting fluid effectively. Testing was conducted using a customdesigned container, and data analysis identified the optimal supply strategy, thereby extending the usable lifespan of the cutting fluid. This system enhances production longevity and allows for the configuration of containers with appropriate capacities based on specific requirements, ensuring consistent and high-quality production.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an AI-Driven Mobile Robot for Managing Poultry Tasks
abstract: This study presents the design of a smart poultry robot aimed at enhancing the efficiency of poultry farming management and improving animal welfare. As the demand for poultry products grows, traditional breeding methods face challenges such as labor shortages and management difficulties. The robot integrates a range of advanced features, including chicken behavior recognition, floor egg collection, dead chicken detection and removal, breaking up the surface of the bedding, and health status inspection. It autonomously navigates and utilizes artificial intelligence technology to identify and mark abnormal chickens, as well as measure their weight. Compared to existing mobile robots, this prototype model is more adaptable and operates stably in the complex environments of poultry houses. Preliminary test results demonstrate that the robot effectively reduces manual labor, enhances management efficiency, and offers a user-friendly solution for agricultural practices.

articleTitle: Multi-Drone Path Planning Using Gradient Descent and Potential Fields For Warehouse Applications
abstract: This study presents an approach for multi-drone path planning in warehouse environments using a combination of the Gradient Descent Method and Artificial Potential Fields (APF). The objective is to ensure efficient and collision-free navigation of multiple drones through complex warehouse spaces, avoiding obstacles such as storage racks. The Gradient Descent method is employed to guide the drones toward their target locations, while the APF technique integrates attractive forces toward the goal and repulsive forces from obstacles to dynamically adjust the drones’ paths. Simulations were conducted using MATLAB to evaluate key parameters such as path length and navigational time, with variations in obstacle configurations. To validate the approach, real-time experimental trials were performed using custom-built drones equipped with Pixhawk flight controllers and obstacle detection sensors. Results from both simulation and experiments demonstrated high accuracy, with an error of less than 5% in path length and navigational time. The findings show that this combined method is effective for autonomous drone coordination in real-world warehouse applications, ensuring safe, efficient, and adaptive navigation.

articleTitle: Multimodal Robotic Manipulation Learning
abstract: The primary issue addressed in this paper pertains to semantic misunderstandings or errors in textual input, leading to inaccurate correspondences between text and images. Such discrepancies hinder the effective utilization of natural language for instructing robotic actions. To mitigate the problem, a framework that retrieval augmented generation semantic analysis with object recognition is proposed to establish accurate mappings between images and textual descriptions. Specifically, the capabilities of transformer models are leveraged to comprehend the semantics of natural language inputs. Subsequently, through object recognition techniques, the alignment of visual cues with corresponding textual representations is facilitated. In the development of a comprehensive framework that seamlessly integrates natural language understanding, object recognition, and sequence-to-sequence modeling for robotic arm planning. By addressing semantic ambiguities and ensuring precise correspondence between textual instructions and visual inputs, our approach enhances the efficacy of human-robot interaction and facilitates more intuitive and accurate robotic task execution.

articleTitle: Adaptive Path Planning and Obstacle Avoidance for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles Using the Indian Spotted Eagle Algorithm
abstract: In the era of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), effective navigation strategies are crucial for ensuring successful operations. These strategies enable UAVs to maneuver through complex environments, avoid obstacles, and reach their destinations efficiently while minimizing energy consumption and travel time. This study introduces a novel bio-inspired optimization technique called the “Indian Spotted Eagle Algorithm (ISEA),” which enhances UAV path planning. The algorithm incorporates Cubic Spline Interpolation to ensure smooth and continuous paths, allowing UAVs to navigate efficiently through challenging environments. The study assesses the performance of ISEA in comparison with other bio-inspired optimization techniques through simulations in similar scenarios. The findings reveal that the proposed method significantly surpasses other methods by reducing path length by up to 37%. Additionally, the convergence results show that ISEA is faster than the compared bio-inspired algorithms, indicating its strong practical applicability.

articleTitle: An Automatic Design Method of Electric Motor Emulator with Graphical User Interface
abstract: This paper proposes an automatic design method for a motor simulator, which consists of resistors and inductors to replace traditional load motors such as dynamometers. This design not only effectively simulates the motor operation under various load conditions but also significantly reduces reliance on complex hardware requirements. The implementation and validation are performed by using MATLAB Simulink simulation. Additionally, through the proposed graphical user interface in MATLAB Simulink, users can quickly obtain parameters of an equivalent circuit for an electric motor emulator. The simulation results demonstrate that performance of the electric motor emulator is very similar to a real motor equipped with a load. The most advantage of the proposed method is very simple implementation, low cost, and easy for testing.

articleTitle: Simulation Verification of Fuzzy Control of Lithium Battery SOC in a Hybrid System of Fuel Cells and Lithium Batteries
abstract: This paper presents the simulation of a hybrid power system combining a fuel cell and a lithium-ion battery. The main power system architecture consists of a 70 kW proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) integrated with a buck/boost converter. Additionally, a 175 kW lithium-ion battery is used as an auxiliary power source at the output stage, providing energy support during high-load conditions. The system is constructed using MATLAB Simulink, simulating the power system architecture of commercially available high-power hydrogen energy hybrid buses. Fuzzy control logic is incorporated to enhance overall system controllability, ensuring stable charging and discharging control of the lithium-ion battery’s State of Charge (SOC) to extend its lifespan. The simulation investigates the fuel cell’s output voltage, current, and power under conditions where the lithium battery’s SOC is regulated.To validate the SOC control method, a series of tests are conducted to assess its effectiveness and feasibility in maintaining optimal SOC levels, demonstrating that the proposed control strategy successfully prevents overcharging and extends battery life under varying load conditions.

articleTitle: Optimal H∞ Adaptive Observer-based Tracking Control of SISO Nonlinear Stochastic Systems with Uncertain Measurement Function and Noise
abstract: In this study, the optimal $H_{\infty}$ adaptive observerbased indirect reference tracking control design is proposed for the uncertain single-input-single-output (SISO) nonlinear stochastic system with nonlinear uncertain measurement function and measurement noise. In contrast to conventional observerbased adaptive control designs that assume exact linear output measurement functions and ignore measurement noise, the proposed method embeds adaptive fuzzy logic system (FLS) in indirect adaptive controller and observer to effectively approximate the nonlinear uncertain system function and measurement function, respectively. Then, the optimal $H_{\infty}$ adaptive observerbased tracking control strategy is proposed to efficiently attenuate the effect of the adaptive fuzzy approximation errors, external disturbance and measurement noise on the tracking error and observation error as small as possible via solving a corresponding linear matrix inequalities (LMIs)-constrained optimization problem. Finally, a simulation example is provided to validate the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Gaze Direction Detection Using Dilated Convolutional Neural Network and Transfer Learning
abstract: In recent years, many eye-tracking related products are developed, focusing on eye movement and gaze tracking. The former mostly uses more expensive wearable or invasive devices, and the latter sometimes needs to utilize 3D feature points of the head, making data collection more cumbersome. Methods using pure RGB images as input are less common and often require a large amount of data. The direction of gaze is affected by many factors, including head posture as people tend to turn their heads in the direction they are looking. This paper proposes a two-stage gaze direction detection network which consists of the prediction of both head posture and gaze direction. The detection of head and eyes are first conducted, followed by the head posture estimation. We expand the receptive field to acquire more detailed pose information by employing the dilated convolution to HOPENet. For gaze direction prediction, dilated convolutional VGG16 is adopted for feature extraction. The head’s facing angle is then incorporated and passed through three fully connected layers to detect the gaze points of the eyes in the images. Due to the lack of public data for evaluation, in this work we create a new image dataset which utilizes an IMU to record the head posture and a projector-camera system to identify the gaze direction. Transfer learning is also employed to compensate for the limited dataset. The experiments using real-scene images have demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed gaze direction detection technique.

articleTitle: MPC-based Optimization Design for 3D Collision Avoidance of a Mobile Manipulator Based-on Obstacle Velocity Estimation
abstract: This paper presents an optimization design of 3D dynamic obstacle avoidance for a mobile manipulator based on model predictive control (MPC). The design enables a mobile manipulator to achieve optimized 3D collision avoidance motion with shorter avoidance path and faster avoidance time. A 3D LiDAR is installed onboard the robot to acquire environmental point cloud and estimate obstacle velocity. The MPC is designed to track an initial 3D path of the mobile manipulator and avoid any static and dynamic obstacles in real time. Experimental results show that the proposed method can simultaneously avoid static and dynamic obstacles in 3D space. Compared with baseline algorithms without velocity estimation, the proposed method reduces the avoidance path length by 8.27% and path execution time by 13.79%.

articleTitle: Local Path Planning of an Autonomous Mobile Robot with Nonholonomic Constraints based on Control Barrier Functions and Elliptical Bounding Box
abstract: Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) deployed in uncertain environments need to dynamically adjust their paths to avoid obstacles unmarked on the maps, such as walking people, moving vehicles, temporarily stacked objects, etc. This paper proposes a local path planner for avoiding obstacles and then returning to the global path. In planning the local path, nonholonomic constraints associated with the driving and steering mechanisms, and limits on the velocity and acceleration of the AMR are satisfied. In addition, a reasonable safety region is guaranteed by applying control barrier functions (CBFs) that use elliptical bounding boxes of obstacles and consider the heading angle of the AMR. Moreover, an artificial potential field (APF) is established to guide the AMR to return to the global path after bypassing the obstacles. Then simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in a complex environment with many static and dynamic obstacles.

articleTitle: Automated Inspection of Flywheel Metallic Objects Using Deep Learning-Based Defect Detection
abstract: In the current industrial era, automated inspection is crucial for maintaining the quality and reliability of manufactured components. Accurate and efficient inspection processes are essential to meet industry standards. This research presents a deep learning-based model integrated with automated inspection hardware for detecting defects in flywheel workpieces. The flywheels, with dimensions of 22.75 cm outer radius, 16.75 cm inner radius, and 6 cm thickness, were inspected to detect holes, scratches, and pitted defects. The model was trained on 1900 images from 38 flywheels and tested on 7, with 40 ground truth defects identified by professional QA from industries. To meet the requirement of inspecting each flywheel within 20 seconds, we designed a hardware system incorporating a stepper motor, camera, and lighting. The deep learning model is based on YOLOv4Tiny, with modifications to the backbone and feature fusion through an improved Feature Pyramid Network (FPN). We evaluated the model using a confusion matrix to determine precision, recall, and accuracy. Our model detected defects as small as 0.5 mm and achieved the highest accuracy at 95% and 40 fps, outperforming YOLOv5, YOLOv6, YOLOv7, and DETR. The optimal motor speed, determined by real-world observation, was 200 RPM, enabling the system to complete the inspection within 20 seconds.

articleTitle: Intelligent Railway Block System Design with Lightweight CNN and RFID
abstract: Obstacles on railways present significant safety risks. In particular, Taiwan Railways (TR) often faces natural and man-made obstructions. While advanced artificial intelligence (AI) models offer precise detection, their high computational demands limit deployment. Thus, lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) models have been developed, balancing detection accuracy with hardware efficiency. Utilizing feature-extracting preprocessing, these models achieve $F 2$ scores above 0.89 and recalls over 0.9, while maintaining computational complexity under 15 MFLOPs and model sizes within 25 kB. This ensures compatibility with standard PCs and low-cost, low-power systems, enabling widespread deployment in regions lacking advanced AI monitoring. Additionally, TR’s aging block and train-tracking systems, which are prone to failures, are enhanced with a power-saving radio frequency identification(RFID) system compatible with the CNN detector and Bluetooth-enabled passenger displays. This modernizes TR’s infrastructure, improving safety operations and travel-information reliability.

articleTitle: Allocation Optimization of Medical Resources in Emergency Departments
abstract: The emergency department (ED) is one of the busiest regions of a hospital and a high patient volume can impact even the most efficient processes. However, when the ED becomes overcrowded, the ability to deliver timely and effective care is compromised, leading to significant clinical repercussions for health systems. Hospital managers are struggling to balance staffing, safety and care in overcrowded EDs. As an important source of care for safety net populations and those without access to other care, EDs must become more collaborative, adaptable and agile to thrive under these difficult conditions. In this research, an algorithm cooperating driving training-based optimization with ordinal optimization is developed to decide the optimal allocation of emergency medical resources. Driving training-based optimization is a human-based metaheuristic approach that mimics the human activity of driving training. The proposed algorithm is presented to decide the optimal allocation of medical resources for minimizing average patient hospital stays and cost of medical waste simultaneously, and satisfy the specified constraints. The experimental results show that the proposed algorithm can obtain stable and best results on optimal allocation of medical resources problems.

articleTitle: Camera-Radar-Based Adaptive Cross Attention Fusion for Multimodal Object Detection
abstract: Advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) necessitate the integration of data from multiple sensors for accurate environmental perception and object detection. However, fusing information from diverse sensors like cameras and radar presents substantial challenges due to inherent differences in data formats and the need for sophisticated fusion strategies. This paper introduces an Adaptive Cross Attention Fusion Module (ACAFM) tailored for the effective fusion of image and millimeter-wave radar data. By leveraging both channel and spatial attention mechanisms, our approach dynamically adjusts feature weighting during the fusion process, significantly improving detection accuracy and system stability. Evaluations on public datasets demonstrate that our method outperforms existing camera-radar fusion techniques, highlighting its robustness in complex and varied scenarios.

articleTitle: A Load Forecasting Model Based on Sequence-to-Image Preprocessing Framework
abstract: The smart grid is currently composed of many distributed energy resources. To manage these sources, Short-Term Load Forecasting (STLF) is regarded as a crucial role in the power dispatching and energy management domain. To improve the performance and accuracy of the STLF, this paper proposes a Sequence-to-Image preprocessing approach and Rolling Forecasting framework (S2I-RF) to help the model better catch the multi-level seasonality of the load series and overcome the cumulative error associated with the multi-step forecasting. To better extract the spatial pattern and the temporal relationship of the load images, a structure of the hybrid neural network model CNN-ConvBiLSTM-ECANet (CCBE-Net) is proposed. The technique can significantly improve the performance of the STLF in real-time or day-ahead forecasting.

articleTitle: Trajectory Learning and Demonstration of a Robot Manipulator Based-on Sensor Fusion from a Hand-held Tool
abstract: This paper presents a programming system for a robot manipulator using a hand-held demonstration tool. In this system, a user holds the self-designed tool to demonstrate a desired motion path, and the robot arm replicates the learned trajectory. The path-demonstration tool, including optical tags (OT) and an IMU, is designed to collect trajectory data from hand motion. Sensor data fusion allows the system to track accurately the demonstrated trajectory. A calibration procedure is proposed to transform the trajectory from tool’s coordinate system to robot’s coordinate system. A cubic spline-based trajectory planning method is proposed to ensure smooth reproduction of the learned trajectory in both time and space. Experimental results show that the robot is able to replicate squared and curved trajectories collected from the path-demonstration tool. The average position error is within 2.435 mm in XYZ directions and the average orientation error is within 0.65 degrees.

articleTitle: LiDAR and Camera Online Calibration Based on a Semantic Reliable Centroid Algorithm
abstract: A novel method for online calibration of cameras and LiDAR extrinsic parameters is proposed. Previous online calibration methods first required offline calibration followed by fine-tuning or optimization online. The proposed online calibration method uses instance segmentation and semantic segmentation to identify common features of camera and LiDAR images and then calculates the centroids of these features to correct the paired points to establish the initial extrinsic parameters. Previous offline calibration is not required. In addition, the problems of angle and point cloud inhomogeneity were considered; the algorithm selects either the contour method or the cluster method to calculate the centroid to maximize the accuracy of the initially calculated extrinsic parameters. These parameters are then optimized using a designed cost function; minimizing the cost function produces the selected extrinsic parameters as the calibration result. The method proposed in this study was evaluated on the Kitti Dataset. The experimental results reveal that the method in this study is feasible in terms of both its initialization strategy and its online calibration accuracy for both the LiDAR and the camera.

articleTitle: Using Layer-wise Depth Recursive Prediction to Predict Underwater Sea Temperature
abstract: The impact of sea temperature (ST) variations on climate and ecosystems is profound, posing not only significant economic losses but also potential threats to life safety. Consequently, accurate ST prediction has become an extremely important research topic. Early ocean observation data were mostly limited to the sea surface, but with the advancement of the Argo program, it is now possible to obtain ST data at various depths. Many studies have focused on predicting ST, commonly employing machine learning and deep learning techniques. However, most of these studies use only surface parameters to predict ST at different depths, leading to a significant decrease in prediction accuracy as depth increases. To address this issue, this paper proposes a method called Layer-wise Depth Recursive Prediction (LDRP). This method first trains a model to predict the ST at the uppermost depth and then uses the prediction results from the upper depth as input for the model at the next depth level, thereby improving the prediction accuracy at subsequent depths. Using data provided by the Argo program, this study combines the LDRP method with a Transformer-based model to train and predict ST at different depths. The experimental results show that the predictions made using the LDRP method exhibit improved accuracy across all depth levels compared to predictions made without LDRP, and the prediction stability at different depths is also significantly enhanced. Overall, this research not only effectively improves the accuracy of ST predictions at various depths but also mitigates the decline in prediction accuracy that occurs with increasing depth in current methods. These results demonstrate the significant potential of the LDRP method for deep ST prediction, and future studies may consider applying this method to even deeper sea temperature predictions to further verify its stability and accuracy.
